A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same spatial-semantic video object segmentation framework. Their complete main texts, equations, tables, figures, and appendices are readable and can be matched despite renumbering and formatting changes.

before.justification: v1 reports original segmentation benchmarks, component ablations, and qualitative results in Tables 1–3, Tables A2–A3, and the accompanying figures.

after.justification: v2 retains original benchmark and ablation results and adds SAM2 comparisons, VOTS2023 results, and internal-feature visualizations.

M1.justification: The semantic embedding, deformable spatial attention, discriminative feature selection, query update, and dual-level memory remain the same. Naming the method S3 and clarifying existing operations do not establish a procedural or architectural change.

E1.justification: v2 adds LVOS V2 validation coverage in Table 4 and extends the VOT material from selected failure cases to a scored VOTS2023 benchmark evaluation. The original five VOS benchmarks and proposed method's training datasets remain.

E2.justification: The comparison set expands substantially through SAM2 Hiera-B+ and Hiera-L in Table 4 and Dynamic_DEAOT, M-VOSTrack, HQTrack, and DMAOT in Table 9. Conversely, STM, AFB-URR, and CFBI disappear from the quantitative benchmark comparisons. JointFormer is retained despite its revised citation and separation of training settings.

E3.justification: New evaluations introduce a 1024p SAM2 comparison with stated model-size controls and VOTS2023 metrics Q, A, R, NER, DRE, and ADQ. Existing training and memory schedules remain; the 480p and 600/720p evaluations are largely reorganized. The YouTubeVOS2018 description changes from 3,471 to 347 training videos without documenting actual subsampling.

E4.justification: Figures 3, 7, and 8 add analyses of stage-wise features, backbone activations, and query–feature similarity. Most existing quantitative ablations survive in Tables 7–8. However, the spatial-only LVOS-val result from v1 Table 1 and one qualitative example from v1 Figure 3 are omitted.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental seed values, repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. Random frame sampling and streaming averages describe the procedure, not statistical uncertainty.

E6.justification: New results include S3's 83.7 on LVOS V2 versus SAM2 Hiera-B+'s 75.8 at 1024p, and VOTS2023 Q=0.67 and R=0.86. Table 3 changes reported speed from 8.0 to 13.1 FPS and Swin-B-AOT-L's LVOS score from 59.4 to 54.4. Table 6 also contains unexplained differences in redisplayed scores. Lower abstract scores mainly select existing 480p results; the earlier high-resolution DAVIS 89.1 and YouTubeVOS2019 88.5 remain.

T1.justification: Equations (1)–(6) preserve the same mathematical operations. Changes such as Q becoming Qin and additional symbol explanations do not revise the underlying mathematics. Neither version adds theoretical propositions or proofs.

C1.justification: Both versions claim that spatial-semantic features and discriminative query propagation improve robustness and achieve state-of-the-art VOS performance across five benchmarks. The S3 name and revised headline numerical examples do not redefine these central contributions.

C2.justification: v2 interprets the new visualizations as showing clearer contours after semantic embedding, stronger object details after spatial modeling, and target-specific query responses. It also identifies inference speed as future work. The existing limitation concerning segmentation of object parts versus whole objects remains.

D1.justification: The abstract changes a promised code/model release into a stated release with a repository link; availability cannot be independently verified from the PDFs. v2 explicitly identifies ViT-base and four spatial-semantic blocks. Most appendix implementation, augmentation, hardware, and memory details remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds the SAM2 reference and comparison discussion, adds Zhang et al. (2023) for JointFormer comparisons, and removes the Liang et al. adaptive feature-bank reference. The broader positioning against matching-based, query-based, and adapter methods remains substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 copyedits and rephrases passages throughout the abstract, introduction, related work, and method descriptions, introduces S3 terminology, moves Limitations into Section 4.4, and adds acknowledgments. The overall narrative and section sequence remain recognizable.

P2.justification: v2 substantially reorganizes the displays: Figure 1 becomes a larger full-width plot, Figure 2 is revised, feature visualizations are added, Table 3 is split across standard-setting and appendix comparisons, and SAM2 and VOTS2023 tables are introduced. Table 1 is condensed, while Table 2 separately redisplays the existing Depth Anything results. Earlier qualitative figures largely survive with renumbering and relocation.

improvement.justification: The new comparisons, feature analyses, and reported code/model release strengthen validation and reproducibility. However, new reporting inconsistencies undermine confidence: Table 6 gives MEGA-trained MOSE 73.2 while Tables 3 and 7 retain 74.0, and the claim of beating SAM2 on every metric contradicts Table 4's MOSE F scores, 79.8 versus 79.9. Table 9 also contains incorrect gain annotations. These unresolved issues make the net quality benefit uncertain.
